findings.rule_id: F5 AC2 (QA O1: approve prod after reading its what-if)
findings.what: WhatIf is a separate job but in the same stage (Deploy_<env>) as the policies-<env> deployment job, so the prod approval is still asked before the what-if runs. QA defect not resolved.
findings.why: Azure DevOps evaluates checks on protected resources per stage. The Approvals and checks docs say that before a stage can begin, all checks on all resources used in that stage must pass. The tester's own O1 (docs/qa/build-F5.md, observation O1) says the same and names the fix: a what-if-only stage before the prod deployment stage. c2af74d moved the what-if into its own job (lines 22-43) inside the stage that consumes environment policies-${{ parameters.environmentName }} (line 56). Deploy_prod therefore pauses for the policies-prod approval before WhatIf starts, which is the defect David ruled fix-now in gate.qa@925fe90. The comment at lines 19-21 ('it runs before any approval is asked for') is false under that model. Certainty: this rests on the documented stage-level check evaluation. I can't verify it against a live Azure DevOps, and nothing in the repo or receipts shows job-level evaluation. The job-level ordering itself is sound: Deploy dependsOn WhatIf; the what-if step downloads the drop and uses the variable group and the ARM connection as a compile-time parameter. It just doesn't come before the approval.

findings.what: The red checker encodes job-level separation in one stage, so it passes on the R1 layout and can't detect the QA defect. Lines 85-86 repeat earlier checks.
findings.why: Lines 74-84 require one regular job running the what-if, no environment on it, no what-if in the deployment job, and dependsOn from the deployment job. They inspect only template['stages'][0]['jobs'] (line 62). Nothing asserts that the what-if runs in a stage that consumes no environment and that the deploying stage depends on it, which is the property the approval timing needs (see R1). The comment at lines 74-75 ('so the approval on policies-prod is given after the what-if exists') claims more than the checks prove. gate.finding-red@6fe2b8d shows the 4 red lines failing for the job-level reasons only. Lines 85-86: the first conjunct is implied by the line-76 filter, and the other two repeat line 72 and line 84. So the 'what-if must come before deployment sub create' assertion adds nothing, though it's not weaker. Routed to builder because the tester can't write infrastructure/** (gate.finding-red@f2065e7).

QA defect status: NOT RESOLVED (R1). The what-if now runs before the Deploy job, but it's still inside the stage that the policies-prod environment approval gates. Under stage-level check evaluation, the approver still approves before any prod what-if output exists.

Checker weakening (6fe2b8d, c2af74d): NONE FOUND, with one caveat. The fix commit edited only stage-template.yml and pipeline.schema.json, per activity 440-444 and `git add` at activity 451. The checker changed only in the red commit, a single builder Edit at activity 432. gate.finding-red@6fe2b8d records the removed lines as the jobs[0] lookup and the in-job what-if<create index check. At HEAD, the deployment job is found by key (line 63, which fails closed via StopIteration if missing). The ordering is re-expressed as what-if outside the deployment job plus dependsOn (lines 76-84). For job-level order that is at least as strong. All the earlier assertions are present unchanged at HEAD: I1-I8, A2/R2, A2/R3, S1 and A2.2/R1. Caveat: I can't run git show, so the old text rests on the gate receipt plus HEAD.

Schema change in c2af74d: the regular-job branch of pipeline.schema.json gains dependsOn, pool and variables, and a `download: current` step is added. Job and step objects still have additionalProperties false with no `condition` or `continueOnError`. That rejects a Deploy with condition: always(), or a what-if step with continueOnError, either of which would bypass the dependsOn. This is a good closure.
